title: Go global
summary: The workforce beyond your borders, without new entities: the international contractor signed and paid, the 1099 added to payroll, the hire abroad employed through an EOR.

parts.title: Hire intl contractor
parts.guidance: Evaluate the proposed international contractor arrangement using the worker's location, actual duties and working relationship. Follow the contractor workflow to review classification, contract, data access and payment requirements before engagement. Document the classification assessment separately from platform onboarding, and carry its outcome into the agreement and payment setup.

parts.title: Add a contractor (1099)
parts.guidance: Use the US-contractor onboarding workflow only when that reporting path fits the worker and payee facts. Reconcile identity, tax documentation and payment details to the approved engagement, and have the appropriate payroll or tax owner resolve foreign-payee exceptions. Save the verified setup privately without assigning a US reporting category merely because another country is involved.

parts.title: Hire abroad via an EOR
parts.guidance: Assess an employer-of-record arrangement against the proposed employee's country, role, compensation and intended start. Review the provider's actual employment, payroll, benefits and termination responsibilities with the relevant advisers before committing. Record the employment and onboarding outcome together with the duties the agreement leaves with the company.
